_readme: Every feature GATE that is OFF unless something turns it on must appear here.
The list of gates is DERIVED by AST (api/services/feature_flag_index.py) and
never typed; tests/test_feature_flag_ledger.py fails BY NAME when a new one
ships without an entry.
Why this exists: a gate that defaults off and is set nowhere is
indistinguishable, from outside the repo, from a gate that is off ON PURPOSE.
PATTERN_VISION_ENABLED=0 was a deliberate retirement; twelve others measured
on 2026-08-30 were simply never decided. Nothing could tell them apart.
status: armed  = set on at least one Railway service (its value is the decision)
dark   = deliberately off; note MUST say why
pending= built, no decision yet; note + since MUST be present
A gate can also be declared as a TABLE - a module-level *_FLAGS dict whose
keys are gate names, read in a loop. feature_flag_index learned that form on
2026-09-12, after Wave K shipped four capabilities the AST could not see:
os.environ.get(env_name) has no string constant to match, so 140 flag tests
passed over a ledger that was four gates short. tests/test_notebook_flag_table_form.py
is the rail, with the control that a bare loop-variable read is still invisible.
This file records INTENT. It cannot see Railway, so it can drift from reality:
run tools/flag_ledger_audit.py to compare it against what is actually set.
build_flags: the BUILD-TIME frontend flags, read in app/src/** as
import.meta.env.VITE_*. They are NOT in `flags` above because that section is
held to a gate list derived by AST from api/** - Python only.
WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS: on 2026-09-12 nine VITE_* were set on the web service,
eight to the literal 1, and ALL NINE had been undefined in the shipped bundle
for four days (Dockerfile.web declared no build ARGs). Nothing in the repo could
see it because nothing in the repo was looking at this half of the app. That was
a structural blind spot, not an oversight.
The name list is DERIVED by tools/vite_flag_index.py and never typed;
tests/test_vite_flag_ledger.py fails BY NAME when a VITE_* ships without a row,
and tests/test_dockerfile_vite_build_args.py holds Dockerfile.web's ARG list to
the same derived set.
baked_value is a MEASUREMENT of the deployed bundle at baked_measured_on, not a
prediction. It goes stale the moment the build changes: the served JS is the
authority, and a flag read as `=== '1'` is false when undefined, which is
indistinguishable from off-on-purpose at every layer except the artifact.
flip_precondition: what must be VERIFIED before a held flag is turned on, and
what turning it on changes for a member. A flag held at 0 with no recorded
precondition is the same ambiguity as an unset one - nobody can tell whether it
is waiting on evidence or was simply forgotten.
decision / decision_reason: recorded when an owner rules on a held flag, so
the ledger says WHY a value is what it is and not merely what it is.
member_facing: {label, where[, payload_key]} marks a gate whose surface a MEMBER
sees (TERM-039). It is the ONE place that names the capability to a member: the
Support page feature-status strip and the Beta mark read these entries through
api/services/feature_status.py and take ON/OFF from the per-request auth payload,
never from status here. payload_key is needed only when the payload key is not
the lowercased flag name. An OFF capability is never listed; declare one only if
its payload key is an explicit false when off (tests/test_feature_status.py).

ARTIFACT_VERSIONS_ENABLED.note: ARMED on web 2026-10-02 16:05Z (owner-run --set; deploy 94d46235 SUCCESS 16:08Z, fresh boot). Verified as the smoke account: /api/artifact-versions/status 200 enabled=true kinds screen/layout/watchlist retain 10. COV-06 (version history on user-authored artefacts), ENABLEMENT GATE, default OFF, read per call in api/services/artifact_versions.py::is_enabled(). SERVICE: web. What it arms: (1) every committed save of a member's saved screen (api/services/screener/saved_screens.py create/update) and of a member's OWN user-scope named chart layout (api/services/charts_layout_service.py upsert) is snapshotted into the artifact_versions table of the TERM-021 store FILE (/data/workspace_docs.db, path read from workspace_doc_store._DB_PATH - same file and nightly backup, its own table; workspace_doc_versions is untouched), after a pre-write baseline of the value the save replaced; (2) GET /api/artifact-versions/{screen|layout}/{id}, GET .../{version} and POST .../restore (compare-and-set on base_version, 409 on a stale base), owner-scoped (somebody else's artefact is 404), screens paid (402); (3) the History control in the Screener's My screens rows and in the /charts Layout Dock's right-click menu, which render nothing unless the list route answers 200. Retention: newest 10 per artefact (Bloomberg MNRS), after coalescing a save superseded by the next save within 60 s (named layouts auto-save ~400 ms after each arrangement change); a baseline, a restore and the version a restore replaced are never coalesced; every removal is recorded in artifact_version_prune_log, and retention runs only while armed. A restore writes the old stored TEXT back verbatim through the artefact's own store and appends it as a NEW version, so it is itself undoable; it never restores a screen's publication (is_public/share_token) or a layout's name. Unset: no I/O, no file opened or created, saves byte-identical, every route 404, the UI control absent (tests/test_artifact_versions.py). NOT ARMED: no owner decision yet; nothing blocks it technically, but STORE_BACKUP must keep covering workspace_docs (it does today). REVERSAL: unset it and redeploy web if the unset does not restart it. The rows are LEFT IN PLACE; never delete them to undo an arming. FOLLOW-UPS (lane/cov-06-10-followups): (a) WATCHLISTS are versioned too (kind 'watchlist', api/services/watchlist_service.py): a whole-list snapshot {name, description, items_json} after every committed edit (add / bulk add / remove / reorder / note / rename), same 60 s coalescing and newest 10; never the flagged shadow list, an admin INDEX list, or a LINKED list. (b) DELETE KEEPS A TOMBSTONE: a delete while armed appends the removed content (baseline first if it was never versioned) and a 'delete' row, so the history outlives the artefact; GET /api/artifact-versions/{kind}/deleted lists them and POST /{kind}/{id}/undelete recreates one under its old id from any kept version, compare-and-set, unpublished / unshared (a layout's live share link is revoked by an appended row). UI: Recently deleted in the Screens menu, the Layout library and Watchlists My Lists; Version history on a list's header menu. No new table. Rails: tests/test_artifact_versions_followups.py, app/src/components/artifactHistory/RecentlyDeleted.test.jsx, app/src/pages/Watchlists.versions.test.jsx.

SERVICE: web (tweet_store reads run in-process on web; the catalyst engine's tweet signal reads the same store). OPTIONS_SCREENER_ENABLED.note: COV-02 (screen the option, not the stock) + COV-03 (market-wide unusual option volume and IV percentile), read ONLY from our own options log. ENABLEMENT GATE, default OFF, read per call in api/services/research/options_screener.py::is_enabled(). TWO SERVICES read it: (1) terminal-next-monitor -- the `options-screen` job (weekdays 16:30 ET, queued after `options-log` in the same cron firing) reads each logged session's contracts file from R2 once and writes options_log/<YYYY>/<date>.volume.csv.gz (per-underlying total/call/put option volume) and <date>.screen.sqlite.gz (screenable contracts with DTE, OTM %, |delta|, spread % precomputed and indexed); it catches up every logged session lacking those files (at most 5 per run). MEASURED 2026-10-02 on the real 2026-09-30 log: 35.6 s to build, screen file 50.8 MB gz / 156.7 MB opened, a whole-universe preset ~0.9 s; and the log's volume column is EMPTY on all 2,018,713 contracts, so the unusual-volume history falls back to the flow tape: the same job writes options_log/tape_volume/<YYYY>/<date>.csv.gz per tape session (last 91, at most 30 per run) from /api/flow/{dates,data,indexes-data} -- the tape keeps only aggregated prints of 50+ contracts and $10K+ premium, which the ranking states in words. Needs DATA_SYNC_* there, plus PUSH_SECRET and OPTIONS_SCREENER_TAPE_URL (or WORKER_INTERNAL_URL) for the tape half; without them the log half still builds and the receipt is an ALERT naming the missing variable. (2) web -- GET /api/options-screener/screen, /unusual-volume, /iv-percentile (paid, plain def, 404 before identity when unset) and the auth payload key options_screener_enabled, present ONLY when on, which mounts the Screener's Options view. The screener queries the LATEST session's prebuilt SQLite file (mirrored once per session, results cached per query); rankings are cached per set-of-sessions. Every row names its session and says end-of-day snapshot. Unusual volume ranks only with >=10 prior logged sessions (else 'n sessions, needs 10'); IV percentile only with >=20 current-rule ATM IV sessions (else the count and the projected date). Pending: owner decides when to arm; the rankings fill as the log accumulates (coverage began 2026-09-30, 2026-10-01 missing). Arm: set OPTIONS_SCREENER_ENABLED=1 on terminal-next-monitor first (builds the files), then on web. Rollback: unset (derived files in R2 stay; nothing else is written).

UNSET/off = exactly today's behaviour (the middleware returns after one env read) - which is why it ships dark. shadow = never blocks; every request is counted and a would-limit is logged ONCE PER (family, key, minute) as '[rate-limit-policy] would-limit mode=shadow family=... prefix=... method=... key=member:<id>|ip:<hash> limit=... retry_after=N family_count=N'; GET /api/admin/rate-limit-policy (admin) serves the counts. enforce = 429 with Retry-After (seconds to the window reset), X-RateLimit-Limit/-Remaining/-Reset and a JSON body naming the family. An unrecognised value is shadow (never blocks, never silent). FAILS OPEN: a limiter error logs and lets the request through. PER-PROCESS: the counters are in-memory, so a second web process doubles every budget. The limits are starting ceilings, not measurements. OWNER STEPS: set shadow on web, read the would-limit lines for a trading week (an ip: key with a huge family_count is usually ONE internal caller without the bearer - the chart-renderer on the render family, a script - give it PUSH_SECRET or raise that family's tier before enforcing), tune the tiers, then set enforce.
